factual_claims.claim: Net interest income declined to 73.3 million euros from 77.6 million euros, reflecting narrower interest margins as market rates dropped, with the six-month Euribor falling to 2.1 percent by year-end.

factual_claims.claim: Growth was propelled by all financing lines, led by a 27 percent increase in business loans amounting to 207 million euros and a 17 percent increase in home loans totaling 125 million euros.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Management report states: 'The business loan portfolio grew the fastest, increasing by €207 million (+27%). This was followed by growth in the home loan portfolio by €125 million (+17%).'

factual_claims.claim: Customer deposits grew by 9 percent to reach 2.05 billion euros, driven by an 11 percent increase in demand deposits and an 8 percent increase in term deposits.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Management report states: 'Coop Pank's deposits increased by 9% over the year, reaching 2.05 billion euros by the end of 2025... Term deposits increased by 8% over the year, while demand deposits increased by 11%.' Note 15 shows customer deposits of 2,047 million euros in 2025 vs 1,877 million euros in 2024 (a 9.07% increase).

factual_claims.claim: A significant strategic milestone during the period was the issuance of 250 million euros in covered bonds on the Irish stock exchange under a new 750 million euro program, providing long-term stable funding that enabled the bank to intentionally reduce reliance on expensive term deposits.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Management report states: 'In the first quarter of 2025, Coop Pank issued covered bonds on the Irish stock exchange for the first time, amounting to €250 million with a four-year maturity. This was the first tranche of a €750 million covered bond program... This stable long-term funding allowed the bank to begin intentionally reducing the volume of more expensive term and foreign deposits.'

factual_claims.claim: Additionally, the bank concluded a synthetic securitization transaction with the European Investment Bank Group to optimize regulatory capital and facilitate up to 249 million euros in new sustainable business loans.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Management report states: 'At the end of the year, Coop Pank entered into a guarantee agreement with the European Investment Bank Group, under which part of the credit risk arising from Coop Pank's loan portfolio will be transferred to EIB Group, thereby providing capital relief to Coop Pank and enabling the bank to issue up to €249 million in new loans to businesses... This is Coop Pank's first synthetic securitization transaction, and also the first such transaction in the Baltics based entirely on the loan portfolio of a single country – Estonia.'

factual_claims.claim: In line with its dividend policy, the bank distributed 7.2 million euros in net dividends, translating to 0.07 euros per share, and proposed a dividend of 0.065 euros per share for the 2025 financial year.

The Management Board of Coop Pank AS proposes to the General Meeting of the Shareholders to allocate the Group’s net profit for the financial year 2025... pay dividends 0.065 euro per share in the total net amount of 6,738 thousand euros.'
